stage: RoPE replacement: pattern fully identified, not implemented
status: assessed; the mechanism the inventory asked for is now written down
why_it_was_deferred: the two replacements that change what runs on the hardware -- attention and the cache write -- are done and verified. RoPE is lower value: the graph already computes it correctly, and replacing it costs three kernels per rotation to save a broadcast multiply.

the_pattern.summary: standard rotate-half RoPE, but spread over twelve ops rather than being one node
the_pattern.cat: CatOp(NegOp(SliceOp(permute_2, dim 3, 64, end)), SliceOp(permute_2, dim 3, 0, 64))  -- rotate_half
the_pattern.sin: SinOp(clone_1); cos is the symmetric SinOp sibling
the_pattern.cos_sin_in_the_shape_the_kernel_wants: the [1, S, 2, 64] tensor that view_3 reshapes to [1, S, 128]; the rope kernel needs [S, 64]

what_a_matcher_would_have_to_do: find an AddOp whose parents are both MulOps, with one sharing a rotate-half sub-pattern (Cat of Neg(Slice(64:)) and Slice(:64)) and the other not
check both muls use the same rotation input
trace the two unsqueezes back to the cos and sin tensors and reshape them to [S, 64] via the pre-view tensor
transpose the rotation input from [1, heads, S, head_dim] to [S, heads, head_dim], which the rope kernel indexes, and transpose the result back
call rope_{S}x{heads}x128(X, Cosine, Sine, Out) and repoint the consumers
kernels_available: rope_16x16x128, rope_1x16x128, rope_16x8x128, rope_1x8x128 -- all four model shapes exist and pass on the board
cost_if_done: three kernels per rotation (transpose in, rope, transpose out), two rotations per layer
the_pattern_is_verified: the reading above was taken from the imported graph by walking parents, not from the model's source

what_it_would_take.matcher: find an AddOp of two MulOps where one shares a rotate-half sub-pattern (Cat of Neg(Slice(64:)) and Slice(:64)) over the same rotation input as the other
what_it_would_take.cos_sin: the graph carries cos and sin as [1, S, 128] -- the 64 frequencies duplicated -- and the kernel wants [S, 64], so each needs a slice of the first half
what_it_would_take.transposes: the rotation input is [1, heads, S, 128] and the kernel indexes [S, heads, 128], so it needs a transpose in and another out; layout_context_{16,8}x{S}x128 and layout_q_{S}x16x128 both exist
what_it_would_take.so: 10 extra kernel calls per layer to replace a broadcast multiply and a concatenate

why_that_is_a_bad_trade_right_now: the graph's RoPE is already correct and verified -- this changes what runs, not whether it is right
the two replacements that change the hardware picture (attention, cache write) are done, verified, and are the ones whose speed effect is actually in question
each replacement so far has cost a debugging cycle on a layout or naming subtlety (the K transpose, the symbol collision); this one has more moving parts than either
the remaining board work -- the full model and stage E -- is the objective's headline and cannot be advanced while the board is busy
cost_benefit.decision: documented in full rather than rushed. The inventory asked for the mechanism for these three; for RoPE that mechanism is now written down precisely enough to be a bounded task.
